transcript.cleaned_text: A man was left with a $1,000 bill after his 6-year-old son ordered a virtual buffet of food from several restaurants last weekend. This led to a string of unexpected deliveries, and maybe a starring role in an advertisement campaign. Keith Stonehouse said the food piled up quickly at his home Saturday night after he let his son use his cell phone to play a game before bed. He said the youngster instead used his father's online food ordering account to order food from one restaurant after another. The boy's mother, Christine Stonehouse, said that the online food app has reached out to the family and offered them a $1,000 gift card. The company also is considering using the family in an online promotional campaign. Most of the food went into the family's refrigerators. They also invited some neighbors over to eat some of it. The father is planning to change his password.

transcript.cleaned_text: Animal behaviour experts looked at more than 100 research papers. They examined how visitors affected the behaviour of more than 250 species in zoos. They found that elephants socialised more with each other during public feeding times. After public feeding times, they were more likely to search for food and less likely to be inactive. In the presence of many visitors, elephants were less likely to use repetitive behaviours which often indicate boredom. Visitors had a similar effect on some other species too, including polar bears, certain jungle cats and black-tailed prairie dogs. Some animal species have been born and raised in zoos, and so have likely become used to the presence of humans. Zoo visitors are often aspects of zoo animals' environment that animals cannot control, and as such can be stressful, although some species appear to show good adaptability to the changing conditions of visitors.

transcript.cleaned_text: Denver is suspending its popular electric bike incentive program. The program was launched in April. It allowed Denver residents to apply for $400 in government funds before buying an electric bike from a participating shop. Residents who met certain income qualifications could qualify for $1,200. More than 3,000 Denver residents applied for incentives within the first three weeks. The city then changed the program to limit the number of applications each month. On Monday, the city announced the pause. We're honored to be a part of transforming the way Denver wants to move around, said Grace Rink, Denver's chief climate officer. We exhausted three years' worth of funding in six months. The city said the program has put 4,400 electric bikes on the streets of Denver and invested $8.6 million into the local economy. The city has provided 2,200 incentives to lower-income residents that represent 68% of the program funding. The city expects to resume the program early next year. It also plans design changes to make participation easier and increase access to the program.

transcript.cleaned_text: Contrary to popular belief, consumers aren't as smart as they like to believe. Many consumers report comparing multiple competing brands and prices when evaluating a purchase. However, research indicates that this is not actually the case. What consumers really think or feel often contradicts what they say. A big reason is that they're driven by unconscious urges, the biggest of which is emotion. Emotion is what really drives the purchasing behaviors and also decision-making in general. Good marketers keep in mind this important fact all the time. And examples of emotion-based campaigns are everywhere. Think for a moment: what is actually being sold in most marketing campaigns? Luxury goods target our feelings of self-worth, acceptance and status in the world. Communication devices excite us by offering a connection to friends, family and a broader network of people. And many other products, such as rings, target emotions related to love and relationships. As marketers, we should focus on the features of the product, but we must also sell the lifestyle and the feeling. The key is to highlight the emotional response a consumer will have by using the product. To achieve the highest emotional response, we should target our consumer through many different senses. A lot of what drives consumers is subconscious behavior. But this isn't a bad thing. There's nothing manipulative about helping consumers achieve desired states of emotion.

transcript.cleaned_text: Plastics have for years been used to make nearly everything that surrounds us, but along the way they escaped the confines of packaging and objects and settled in the environment, the food we eat and the air we breathe. Americans are consuming and breathing in a lot of plastic. Based on available data, Americans take in an estimated 74,000 to 121,000 microplastic particles every year. However, scientists believe the true number is probably much higher because for some likely sources of microplastics, there was no strong data available. Microplastics get into food and air in several ways. Many start off as part of larger plastic objects, which over time fragment into smaller and smaller pieces until they become tiny, five millimeters or less in diameter. They are breathed in or consumed by animals that then become our food. The particles float through the air until people breathe them in. They also settle on the food that people eat. Data shows that for Americans, air, bottled water and seafood were the biggest sources for breathed-in or consumed microplastics. Added sugars accounted for less, and salts, tap water and beer contributed minimal amounts. These estimates are conservative. The included foods only make up about 15% of the average American diet. It's not yet known how much plastic is contained in the remaining 85% of the typical diet.

transcript.cleaned_text: People looking to stay well as they age may want to adopt a pet animal, according to new data from the University of Michigan National Poll on Healthy Aging. For the survey, researchers polled about 2,000 US adults from ages 50 to 80. 55% said they owned at least one pet. Dogs were the most common pet, followed by cats. But whatever the type of animal, the vast majority of owners said their pets boosted their mental and physical health. Nearly 90% of older pet owners said their animals helped them enjoy life and feel loved. Roughly 80% said their pets reduced stress, and almost three quarters said their pets provided a sense of purpose. However, people did report a few disadvantages to pet ownership. These included difficulty traveling and financial strains. 6% of pet owners said they'd fallen or injured themselves as a result of having a pet. Still, plenty of research has shown that just about anyone can benefit from their pet since animals can lower stress, reduce symptoms of depression and anxiety, and encourage physical activity. The new poll suggests that pet ownership may be especially beneficial for older adults, given how common loneliness and social isolation are within this age group. Human social support comes with a host of health benefits: less stress, lower rates of long-term disease, and more. And research shows that interacting with pets can bring many of the same benefits.

options.text_en: Get familiar with all the details of his job description.

options.label: B
options.text_en: Learn about the relations within the organization.

options.label: C
options.text_en: Recognize his own limitations and weaknesses.

options.label: D
options.text_en: Understand his role from various perspectives.

questions.question_text: What does the man say he is feeling a bit uneasy about?

options.label: A
options.text_en: Learning history.

options.label: B
options.text_en: Meeting his boss.

options.label: C
options.text_en: Creating reports for other departments to use.

options.label: D
options.text_en: Leaving his coworkers in the present company.

questions.question_text: What does the woman suggest the man do to gain insight about the running of the business?

options.label: A
options.text_en: Get to know the decision-makers.

options.label: B
options.text_en: Acquire decision-making authority.

options.label: C
options.text_en: Promote its products and services.

options.label: D
options.text_en: Observe its overall management.

questions.question_text: What does research indicate about many consumers when they evaluate a purchase?

options.label: A
options.text_en: They do not tell marketers their feeling about a product.

options.label: B
options.text_en: They do not compare competing brands and prices.

options.label: C
options.text_en: They are not hesitant to contradict themselves.

options.label: D
options.text_en: They are not sure what they really like to buy.

questions.question_text: What do good marketers keep in mind all the time?

options.label: A
options.text_en: Consumers are often attracted by new products.

options.label: B
options.text_en: Consumers tend to make decisions on the spot.

options.label: C
options.text_en: Consumers find it hard to resist temptation.

options.label: D
options.text_en: Consumers are actually driven by emotion.

questions.question_text: What should marketers do besides stressing the features of a product?

options.label: A
options.text_en: Draw consumers’ attention to the luxury goods symbolizing quality life.

options.label: B
options.text_en: Leave consumers the impression they are doing nothing manipulative.

options.label: C
options.text_en: Highlight the emotional response it will trigger in the consumer.

options.label: D
options.text_en: Remind consumers of the wide connections it can help to build.

questions.question_text: What does the passage say about Americans?

options.label: A
options.text_en: They are taking in a lot of plastic.

options.label: B
options.text_en: They are polluting the environment.

options.label: C
options.text_en: They consume much processed food.

options.label: D
options.text_en: They make everything with plastics.

questions.question_text: What counted as the biggest sources for Americans breathing in or consuming microplastics?

options.label: A
options.text_en: Beer, salts and added sugars.

options.label: B
options.text_en: Tap water and take-away food.

options.label: C
options.text_en: Food packages and plastic bags.

options.label: D
options.text_en: Air, bottled water and seafood.

questions.question_text: What does the passage say is still unknown?

options.label: A
options.text_en: How much plastic there is in the remaining 85% of Americans’ typical diet.

options.label: B
options.text_en: What measures can be taken to prevent plastic objects from fragmenting.

options.label: C
options.text_en: What harm microplastics may actually do to the average Americans.

options.label: D
options.text_en: How many ways there are for microplastics to get into food and air.

questions.question_text: What did over half of the respondents say in the survey?

options.label: A
options.text_en: They planned to adopt a pet animal.

options.label: B
options.text_en: They kept not only a dog but a cat.

options.label: C
options.text_en: They had at least one pet.

options.label: D
options.text_en: They liked cats more than dogs.

questions.question_text: What did most older pet owners in the survey say their pets provided?

options.label: A
options.text_en: A sense of pride.

options.label: B
options.text_en: A sense of duty.

options.label: C
options.text_en: A sense of purpose.

options.label: D
options.text_en: A sense of security.

questions.question_text: What does the passage say people did report in the survey?

options.label: A
options.text_en: A few problems with keeping big animals.

options.label: B
options.text_en: Some disadvantages related to pet ownership.

options.label: C
options.text_en: A few cases of getting attacked by pet animals.

options.label: D
options.text_en: Some conflicts with neighbors due to pet keeping.

questions.question_text: What does research show interacting with pets can do?

options.label: A
options.text_en: Reduce as many symptoms of depression as medical help.

options.label: B
options.text_en: Improve people’s health as much as physical activities.

options.label: C
options.text_en: Lower older people’s stress as effectively as exercising.

options.label: D
options.text_en: Bring many of the same benefits as human social support.
